Q: Read file as an array of lines, in Java A:

Files.readAllLines & List#toArray

You can also use java.nio.file.Files to read an entire file into a List of String objects. Then you can convert it to an array.

Assuming a String variable named filePath, the following 2 lines will do that:

List<String> strList = Files.readAllLines(Paths.get(filePath), Charset.defaultCharset());
String[] strarray = strList.toArray(new String[0]);

We can make a one-liner of that code, if so desired.

String[] names = 
    Files
        .readAllLines(                       // Defaults to UTF-8 character encoding in Java 8+.
            Paths.get( "path/to/data.txt" )
        )                                    // Returns a `List of `String` objects. 
        .toArray(new String[0]);             // Puts the `String` objects into an array.

Q: Convert string in iso8601 format to datetime A:

Another padding with strptime().

'2026-04-02T02:16-04:00' |> ## datetime_str
  sub(pattern='(..)([+-]..):(..)$', replacement='\\1:00\\2\\3', x=_) |> 
  strptime(format='%FT%T%z', tz='UTC') 

[1] "2026-04-02 06:16:00 UTC"

You might want to skip the tz-specification.

Q: How can I bypass the ASLR c code that was compiled as 64-bit? (school assignment : “within 10 minutes.”) A:

you cant, at least not in the same way. brute-forcing ASLR was sometimes practical on 32-bit, but not on a normal 64-bit binary. without an information leak or some implementation weakness, there is no realistic 10-minute bypass here

Q: What's the difference between the TMP Input Field Line Types `MultiLineSubmit` and `MultiLineNewline`? A:

SingleLine is of course trivial: No multi lines & Enter = submit

MultiLineSubmit: Enter = submit & Shift + Enter = new line instead. Additionally on mobile phone (or in general soft-) keyboards you usually will only see the submit key and new line might be hidden/unavailable.

MultiLineNewLine afaik means: Enter = new line & There is no built-in submit key => Instead you usually handle the submitting rather via a secondary additional UI button or code explicitly. On mobile phone keyboards you usually will see the normal new line key and no submit

It's mainly about how you handle e.g. the onSubmit event vs cancelling input etc.
